evidence: tools/reach_check.py:1192-1194 `if function not in graph.book_defs: unresolved.append((row["id"], name, f"declared subject {function} is not a book definition"))`; :1202-1204 `unresolved.append((row["id"], name, "no such defthm here"))`; :1208-1210 `"no resolvable subject"`; :1402 `return 1 if (arguments.strict and (fresh or untriaged)) else 0` (unresolved never enters the verdict, only a count in --summary). :1289-1290 prints an unreadable file and continues.
fix: Count unresolved events, and any graph.unreadable entry, as failures under --strict, except where a baseline entry names them with a disposition, the way untriaged orphans are handled. A deliberately host-only subject then gets an explicit HOST disposition instead of a silent bucket.

reviewer: In code, unresolved events never enter the --strict verdict (reach_check.py:1192-1210, :1402), and unreadable books are only printed (:1289-1290). Most of the named scenarios are still caught by sibling steps in the same `make check`. keystone_emit.py --check (Makefile:2763) runs subject_findings (keystone_emit.py:133-160), which fails if :subject is not a function the conclusion calls or if no host line reaches it. ledger.py --check (Makefile:2401) runs validate_events/check_theorem_event (ledger.py:3943-3946), which fails on 'no such theorem'. The remaining uncovered class is non-keystone events whose subject inference yields nothing ('no resolvable subject'), plus books that callgraph cannot read but ledger's reader can. reach_check alone is weaker than AGENTS.md implies, but the composed gate closes most of the gap.
scenario: A defkeystone's :subject is renamed, or is a function generated by a macro that callgraph does not read (a defrecord accessor or a defabsstobj export of a generic not mapped). keystone_emit regenerates keystone_subjects, and reach_check files the event under "unresolved". Likewise, a book callgraph cannot read (graph.unreadable) drops all its definitions and theorems, so its events become "no such defthm here". In each case the reachability gate AGENTS.md cites ("reach_check --strict") exits 0 without checking whether a host line reaches the keystone's subject. That is the exact property the gate exists to enforce.
title: reach_check --strict passes registry events it cannot resolve (stale declared subject, missing defthm, unreadable book)
